name: Half Marathon — Intermediate

workouts.name: 7km Easy Run
workouts.description: Relaxed aerobic run at conversational pace. Builds base fitness.
workouts.notes: Readiness has been sliding all week (80 to 11 over the last six days, sleep only 40 last night) and today's status reads Recovery — this is a real fatigue signal, not noise. You already ran an easy 5K this morning instead of the planned hill reps, which was the right call; this entry now matches what actually happened. The hill work isn't lost, just postponed until readiness rebounds.

briefing.purpose: Aerobic base — most of your fitness is built here, at an effort that lets you absorb the hard days instead of digging the hole deeper.
briefing.feel: Conversational, RPE 3-4. You should finish feeling like you could do it again.
briefing.if_wrong: If pace drifts above the window to hold a conversation, let it — easy means effort, not a number. Heart rate above ~75% max: slow down.
briefing.cue: Cadence: count 30 right-foot strikes in 20s (target creeping up over the plan) — quicker, shorter steps, no overstriding.

workouts.name: 4km Tempo Run
workouts.description: Sustained threshold-pace effort. Develops lactate clearance and mental focus.

steps.description: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace

briefing.purpose: Lactate threshold — raises the pace you can sustain. The single biggest lever for Base-phase fitness at your distance. Right now this is groundwork — economy and resilience for the harder blocks ahead.
briefing.structure: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:50-5:19/km → 4 km tempo at threshold pace @ 4:18-4:32/km → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:50-5:19/km
briefing.feel: Comfortably hard, RPE 7. You could speak a sentence, not hold a chat.
briefing.if_wrong: Too hard? Slow 5-10 s/km rather than stopping — the aerobic stimulus survives a slower tempo, not a broken one. Heat or hills: switch to effort.
briefing.cue: Lock the rhythm with your breathing (e.g. 2:2) and let pace follow it.

workouts.name: 13km Long Run
workouts.description: Steady long run building endurance and mental toughness at easy pace.

briefing.purpose: Endurance — time on feet grows capillaries, fat metabolism and durability. Unstructured on purpose: no targets, run to feel, switch off.
briefing.feel: Relaxed, conversational. The watch stays quiet today — that's the point.
briefing.if_wrong: Fading late is normal early in a plan; walk breaks beat abandoning. Feeling great ≠ speed up — save it for the structured long runs.
briefing.cue: Check posture every ~15min: tall hips, relaxed shoulders, quiet feet.

weeks.intro: Base week 1 of 2: laying aerobic foundation and durable form — economy work now makes every later phase cheaper.

workouts.name: 10 x 200m Speed Reps
workouts.description: Short, fast repetitions developing speed and running economy. Full recovery between reps.

steps.description: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace

briefing.purpose: Speed and running economy — short, fast reps recruit fast-twitch fibres and sharpen form, making every slower pace cheaper. Right now this is groundwork — economy and resilience for the harder blocks ahead.
briefing.structure: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:50-5:19/km → 10× (200m fast & relaxed — mile race effort @ 3:41-3:57/km / 60s walking rest @ 4:50-5:19/km) → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:50-5:19/km
briefing.feel: Fast, springy and light — ~95%, never an all-out sprint. Full recovery is part of the design; R work only counts when you're fresh for each rep.
briefing.if_wrong: Form breaking (shoulders up, overstriding)? Stop the set — junk reps train junk form. These reps are about quality, never volume.
briefing.warmup: After the easy warm-up: 2-3 drills (high knees, A-skips) plus 2-3 strides — fast reps on a cold engine is how calves tear.
briefing.cue: Think 'fast feet on hot coals' — ground contact short, heels never settling.
briefing.venue: Track or a measured flat stretch — GPS pace lies over 200-400m, so run these by effort and check splits after.

workouts.name: 9km Easy + 6 Strides
workouts.description: Easy run finishing with short strides to develop running economy and neuromuscular coordination.

briefing.purpose: Easy volume plus neuromuscular priming — strides teach fast, relaxed turnover without fatigue, and set up the next quality day.
briefing.structure: 8.8 km easy @ 4:50-5:19/km → 6× (Stride — fast & relaxed @ 3:41-3:57/km / 45s walking rest @ 4:50-5:19/km)
briefing.feel: Easy throughout; strides are fast and springy, ~90% effort, never sprinted.
briefing.if_wrong: Strides feeling forced or heavy-legged? Cut them — the easy running is the session; strides are a bonus.
briefing.cue: Strides are turnover practice: quick light steps, arms driving straight back, eyes up.

workouts.name: 15km Progressive Long Run
workouts.description: Start easy, build to marathon pace, finish at threshold. Develops pacing and fatigue resistance.

briefing.purpose: Endurance plus fatigue-resistance — running strong in the back half is exactly the race-day skill, trained under control.
briefing.structure: 8.9 km easy @ 4:50-5:19/km → 4.4 km at marathon pace @ 4:30-4:47/km → 1.5 km at threshold pace @ 4:18-4:32/km
briefing.feel: Patient early, purposeful late. The final segment is honest work, RPE 6-7.
briefing.if_wrong: If the faster segments break form, back off to the slow edge of the window — finishing strong matters more than the split.

weeks.focus: 10 x 200m Speed Reps + 15km Progressive Long Run + 15km Progressive Long Run
weeks.intro: Base week 2 of 2: laying aerobic foundation and durable form — economy work now makes every later phase cheaper.

workouts.name: 8 x 60s Hill Reps
workouts.description: Hill repetitions build strength, power, and running economy. Effort should be hard but controlled.

steps.description: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace

briefing.purpose: Strength, power and economy — uphill running loads the posterior chain at low impact and forces a strong knee drive. This is the meat of the build: each week stacks a little more than the last.
briefing.structure: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:50-5:19/km → 8× (60s hard uphill effort / 90s walking rest @ 4:50-5:19/km) → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:50-5:19/km
briefing.feel: Hard but controlled, RPE 8 — effort-based, forget pace on a gradient.
briefing.if_wrong: Calves or achilles complaining? Shorten the reps and stay tall — lean from the ankles, not the waist.
briefing.cue: Drive the knee, push the ground away, arms compact — and walk the first 20m of each descent before jogging.
briefing.venue: Find a steady 4-6% gradient that takes 45-75s to climb; grass or trail saves the calves.

workouts.name: 30min Fartlek
workouts.description: Unstructured speed play — alternate between hard surges and easy running by feel.

steps.description: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace

briefing.purpose: Speed play — unstructured surges build gear changes and make hard running feel playful again. Deliberately loose. This is the meat of the build: each week stacks a little more than the last.
briefing.structure: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:50-5:19/km → 4× (2 min hard surge @ 4:18-4:14/km / 120s walking rest @ 4:50-5:19/km) → 6 min easy jog to finish @ 4:50-5:19/km
briefing.feel: Surges roughly threshold-to-5K effort, by feel. Have fun with it.
briefing.if_wrong: If every surge becomes a time trial, you've missed the point — vary them, land some easy ones.

workouts.name: 16km Long Run w/ 7km Race Pace
workouts.description: Long run with a sustained race-pace block to build specificity and confidence.

steps.description: 15 min easy jog at conversational pace

briefing.purpose: Race specificity — goal pace on tired legs, plus a dress rehearsal for pacing, fueling and kit.
briefing.structure: 15 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:50-5:19/km → 4.8 km easy @ 4:50-5:19/km → 7 km at race pace @ 4:12-4:23/km → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:50-5:19/km
briefing.feel: Race-pace block should feel controlled and rhythmic, not desperate — lock in after 1km and relax into it.
briefing.if_wrong: Can't hold the window without straining? Shorten the block rather than slowing the whole run — quality of pace beats quantity today.
briefing.fuel: Fuel it: carbs beforehand, then practice race-day intake — a gel every ~25-30min and sips of fluid. The gut is trainable; race day is not the day to find out.

weeks.focus: 30min Fartlek + 16km Long Run w/ 7km Race Pace + 16km Long Run w/ 7km Race Pace

workouts.name: 5 x 2.5min VO2max Intervals
workouts.description: Hard intervals at VO2max intensity to raise aerobic ceiling. Full recovery between reps.

steps.description: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace

briefing.purpose: Aerobic ceiling — short hard reps at ~3K-5K effort push maximal oxygen uptake, which everything below it hangs from. This is the meat of the build: each week stacks a little more than the last.
briefing.structure: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:50-5:19/km → 5× (2.5 min hard — 3K-5K race effort @ 3:55-4:14/km / 2.5 min recovery jog @ 4:50-5:19/km) → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:50-5:19/km
briefing.feel: Hard, RPE 8-9. Controlled discomfort — the last rep matches the first.
briefing.if_wrong: Fading before the final rep: slow 5 s/km or take 30s more recovery. In heat or wind run by RPE 8 — the pace window assumes calm, flat ground.
briefing.warmup: After the easy warm-up: 2-3 drills (high knees, A-skips) plus 2-3 strides — fast reps on a cold engine is how calves tear.
briefing.cue: Relax the face and hands on the back half of each rep — tension is free speed lost.

workouts.name: 11km Progressive Run
workouts.description: Start easy, finish fast. Each third gets progressively faster developing pacing discipline.

briefing.purpose: Pacing discipline — each third faster teaches negative splitting, the highest-percentage race strategy there is. This is the meat of the build: each week stacks a little more than the last.
briefing.structure: 3.6 km easy @ 4:50-5:19/km → 3.6 km at marathon pace @ 4:30-4:47/km → 3.6 km at threshold pace @ 4:18-4:32/km
briefing.feel: First third annoyingly easy, last third honest work. Smooth gear changes.
briefing.if_wrong: If the final third isn't the fastest, the start was too quick — that's the exact race-day error this session exists to fix.
briefing.cue: Change gear with cadence first, stride length second.

workouts.description: Race-specific intervals at race pace. Builds confidence and specificity.

steps.description: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace

briefing.purpose: Race specificity — goal pace becomes automatic through repetition. Rhythm, relaxation and confidence at the pace that matters. Race-sharpening territory — quality stays, fatigue drains away.
briefing.structure: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:50-5:19/km → 3× (1.0 km at race pace @ 4:12-4:23/km / 90s walking rest @ 4:50-5:19/km) → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:50-5:19/km

briefing.if_wrong: Consistently outside the window at honest effort: log it — the adaptive review uses exactly this signal to adjust your paces.
